texts: On day 131 of Year 1, a second cold snap came.
The cold wind was unusually sharp that night.
Three lanterns on the Cliff Path went out before dawn.
The three lanterns held salt-bloom in their mire-essence.
The three lanterns went out despite the salt-bloom.
The Council recorded the night as an extreme cold event.
Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the feather store held four weeks of supply.
The wraith response had used half of the autumn feather store.

sentences: On day 131 of Year 1, a second cold snap came.
The cold wind was unusually sharp that night.

q1_issues.issue: Thematic roles lists "use" explicitly under Theme (object acquired/possessed/used with no change to it), so (Patient sk_use_1 sk_portion_1) assigns the wrong direct-object role.

The sealed complement "the feather store held four weeks of supply" is collapsed into a Measure atom instead of being parsed "as usual" into a reified hold event, which the instruction set's own stative-transitive example ("the tank holds forty litres" takes Agent) shows is an event with a class and roles; the event, its class and its subject role are all lost.
"recorded the night as an extreme cold event" asserts (Member sk_night_1 extreme_cold_event) flatly at top level, stating the Council's classification as an unattributed fact.

(Inheritance extreme_cold_event cold) and (Inheritance extreme_cold_event extreme) expose modifiers that are not adjectival properties of the event — "extreme cold" is the noun phrase modifying "event", and a noun modifier is never exposed as a genus.

"despite the salt-bloom" takes an NP complement, but Despite's second argument is pointed at the S4 holding event sk_hold_1, an eventuality the PP does not name (the NP's own symbol sk_salt_bloom_1 is what the text supplies).

q2_gaps: "V NP as NP" predicative complement ("recorded the night as an extreme cold event") — no rule covers a classificatory/naming secondary predicate; only the passive "is considered/said to be" form is addressed, and the resultative shapes do not fit

a concessive/adversative connective with a NOMINAL object ("went out despite the salt-bloom") — Inter-clause connectives requires two reified clauses as endpoints, and nothing licenses a concessive PP over an NP
coreference to a day-part time: "that night" is stored as the bare Time symbol night, so the later argument NP "the night" (a participant, needing an entity symbol) has no antecedent to reuse

past-perfect anchoring across sentence boundaries — the ordering test is worded "whenever the SENTENCE contains another asserted event" while its exception is worded "no other event in the TEXT", leaving "had used" in a standalone sentence of a multi-event passage undecided
review.notes: Strong on the mechanical constructions: "that night" term-propagation from the day-131 antecedent, go_out kept whole as a phrasal verb, the counted-group + per-member distribution rules, (TimeAtMost e dawn) for "before dawn", the entity-attached On for "on the Cliff Path", and the mass-partitive PartOf/ProportionOf shape for "half of the ... store" are all as specified. Event coreference is also good — S5 reuses sk_go_out_1 rather than minting a second going-out.

issues.reason: 'use' is listed verbatim in the Theme gloss (objects acquired, transferred, moved, possessed, perceived or evaluated with no change to them — 'choose, keep, use'), and the fallback rule is 'when the test is unclear, default to Theme', so (Patient sk_use_1 sk_portion_1) breaks the fixed verb-to-role assignment the instruction set imposes precisely so a verb takes the same role in a statement and in its question.

A sealed complement must be 'parsed as usual (classes, roles, tense)' before sealing, and the instruction set's own stative-transitive example is this very verb ('the tank holds forty litres' still takes Agent), so collapsing 'the feather store held four weeks of supply' into a bare Measure atom drops the licensed hold event, its class and its subject role — the same parse reifies 'the lanterns held salt-bloom' correctly three sentences earlier.

The half that stands is the attribution loss — nothing ties the classification to the recording event — but the flat atom is not an unlicensed over-assertion: 'V NP as NP' is uncovered (the reviewer's own gap), the nearest precedent in the instruction set is mid-discourse naming ('She named it Rex' adds the Name atom to the referent at top level), and the passage itself makes (Member sk_night_1 extreme_cold_event) true of the sentence's content.

The half that stands: on the 'extreme cold' + 'event' reading, cold is a noun modifier of a night_shift-type compound and (Inheritance extreme_cold_event cold) is not licensed; the half that falls: neither atom is false or over-asserted — the parse uses cold as a property throughout ((Member sk_wind_1 cold), (Inheritance cold_snap cold)), and extreme is a gradable adjective predicable of the referent, which is the exposure case the rule names.

A connective atom relates two reified eventualities, so the entity sk_salt_bloom_1 would be the ill-typed endpoint while sk_hold_1 — the salt-bloom-holding the previous sentence asserts — is the eventuality the concession actually runs against; the construction (concessive PP over an NP) is the reviewer's own q2 gap, and this improvised endpoint is true of the sentence's content.

gaps_confirmed: 'V NP as NP' classificatory/predicative secondary complement ('recorded the night as an extreme cold event') — no rule covers it; only the passive 'is considered/said to be' form and the resultative shapes exist, and neither fits

concessive/adversative connective with a NOMINAL object ('went out despite the salt-bloom') — Inter-clause connectives requires two reified eventualities as endpoints and nothing licenses a concessive PP over an NP

a time referred back to as a participant ('that night' stored as the bare Time symbol night, then 'the night' as an argument NP) has no licensed way to be typed and tied to its earlier Time-term mention, since the Time section bars minting a witness or Member atom for a time

past-perfect anchoring across sentence boundaries — the ordering test says 'whenever the sentence contains another asserted event' while its exception says 'no other event in the text', leaving a standalone past-perfect sentence inside a multi-event passage undecided
new_gaps: A coverage/endurance quantity ('four weeks of supply', 'three days' worth of fuel') has no licensed Measure scale or unit: the weeks measure how long the stock would last, not a dimension of the store or of the supply, so even the compliant reified hold event leaves the object NP's quantity without a licensed encoding — the fix for issue 1 restores the event but not this figure.
adjudication.defect_summary: For the 'used half of the store' clause the compliant form is (Theme sk_use_1 sk_portion_1), since the instruction set lists 'use' under Theme. For the sealed report complement the compliant form is the ordinary reified event inside the seal — (And (Member sk_hold_2 hold) (Agent sk_hold_2 sk_feather_store_1) (Theme sk_hold_2 <supply-witness>) (Past sk_hold_2)) — per 'parse P as usual' and the 'tank holds forty litres' stative-transitive precedent; note that the '(four weeks) of supply' quantity itself has no licensed carrier, filed as a new gap.
adjudication.notes: Both confirmed issues are role/form discipline rather than false content — every atom in this parse is true of the passage. The mechanical constructions are strong: term-propagated 'that night', go_out kept whole, counted group plus per-member rules, (TimeAtMost e dawn), entity-attached On, the mass-partitive PartOf/ProportionOf shape, and event coreference back to sk_go_out_1.
